trust_decision.summary: An untrusted item name is treated as plain text. It must not be compiled as a regular expression or reach a regex that backtracks catastrophically. At the pinned commit, a usable-item target taken from the name is put unescaped into a dynamic RegExp in decomposeName.

landing_point.why: The advisory names ReDoS in parseString, the main public parsing API; it calls Attributes and then decomposeName.

fix_sites.entry_point: Format.parseString / static parseString, Format.fixName, Format.parseEconItem (via ItemName.getShort)

econ description parser (inferred site, not confirmed by diff)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/parseEconItem/ParsedEcon/ItemName.ts:46 (econ market_name reaches the same decomposeName sink outside parseString)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The econ-item path takes market_name from Steam's inventory API, which a solver could call trusted, unlike a free-form string given to parseString.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Kit/Fabricator/Strangifier/Unusualifier target removal must still strip the target with either a leading or a trailing space, including names with regex metacharacters such as apostrophes, dots or parentheses (e.g. "Killer's"). Rejecting or over-sanitising those names breaks parsing.
